candidates.title: The advantage attributed to pretraining distillation may exceed what the component ablations isolate
candidates.observed_fact: The related-work discussion states that general-purpose pretraining distillation was found beneficial rather than task-specific distillation, and contrasts the method with smaller students trained using the original pretraining objective. The method also uses teacher-layer initialization and modified BERT training practices. The ablation prose describes changes to individual loss components and initialization; the extracted table lists individual loss removals and random initialization. Removing either distillation loss individually leaves another teacher-derived loss in place. Separately, the SQuAD experiment adds task-specific distillation after pretraining distillation.
candidates.suspected_problem: These comparisons support the utility of individual components within the proposed training procedure, but may not isolate the overall advantage of pretraining distillation over a matched compact model trained without distillation signals, or over a task-specific distillation strategy. In particular, individual loss removals do not by themselves establish the combined benefit of both distillation losses relative to masked-language-model pretraining with the same architecture and initialization. The SQuAD addition tests a complementary second stage rather than the stated alternative between distillation stages.
candidates.why_it_matters: The central contribution is a transferable compact model obtained through pretraining distillation. Establishing that the complete recipe works is distinct from establishing which training stage or teacher-transfer mechanism produces its advantage. If the comparative evidence is narrower than the related-work wording suggests, the contribution should be interpreted as a successful integrated recipe with component-level evidence, while its advantage over alternative compression and training strategies remains unresolved.
